li: Heads-up — seeing repeated Xid 13 spikes on gpunode-ax4 (us-west2) over the last 12m. ECC corrected count also trending up. Node is currently in production serving Dedicated pools. Thinking we should try a 'soft-fence' workflow instead of immediate full replace: taint -> graceful evict -> isolation -> escalate to replace if errors persist. Thoughts?

infra-bot: ALERT: [1792004318] host=gpunode-ax4 region=us-west2 metric=XID_ERRORS delta=6 window=12m ECC_CORRECTED_DELTA=240
logs:
```
[GPU0] Xid 13 at 0x7fae... GPU0
[GPU0] ECC corrected 102 -> 342
```

sam: How many active pods/jobs on that node? any long-running training jobs that'll get killed by a drain?

li: ~8 pods, 3 are long-running training jobs in Dedicated. Slurm jobs: none on that host (we're k8s for this pool). If we soft-fence with a longer grace period we can let the training checkpoint.

maya: +1 for soft-fence. Suggest sequence and flags:
1) add taint: `kubectl taint nodes gpunode-ax4 gpu-fence=investigate:NoSchedule`
2) cordon and evict with max-grace: `kubectl drain gpunode-ax4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=600 --timeout=15m`
3) if eviction stalls > 20m escalate to `kubectl drain --force` or create a replacement node
Also route new scheduling to a fallback pool with lower-priority preemptible instances.

oscar: For nodes in Slurm-managed racks we should do similar but use scontrol to set state=DRAIN with Reason and decide requeue vs migrate. Example: `scontrol update NodeName=gpunode-ax4 State=DRAIN Reason="gpu-health:spike"`
If we requeue, ensure we cap backfill so we don't overwhelm backup capacity.

dave: A couple operational guardrails:
- filter transient noise: require either Xid error spikes >=3 within 10m OR ECC_corrected_delta >=200 within 5m.
- do not trigger automated replace for first occurrence: implement exponential backoff per node (1st auto-fence = isolate, 2nd within 24h -> mark for replace).
- add kernel oops / GPU reset detection as hard signal to bypass grace.

li: Agree. We should also track downstream impacts: checkpoint success rate, job restart counts, and tokenized cost of fallback nodes. Propose canary rollout to 5% of nodes in us-west2 for 48h behind a feature flag. Will open a change request PR and a runbook update.

sam: I can pick up the canary deployment and PR for the controller logic (signal combiner + backoff). Will also add a metric (fence_success_ratio) to console dashboards. Please add oncall playbook note.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-3472: "gpu-fence soft-quarantine flow + heuristics" assigned to @sam. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INFRA-3472 :thumbsup:

maya: I'll update the runbook with the exact k8s/slurm commands and include the threshold examples. We should also add a one-click rollback for the feature flag.

li: Thanks — can we sync tomorrow 10:30 PT to sign off on thresholds and rollout percentage? @oncall please review once PR is up.

oscar: noted. I'll add capacity simulation to the scheduler test suite to see how fallback pools behave under a 10% fence rate.

dave: one more: add enrichment to alerts with historical Xid/ECC trend so the oncall doesn't have to dig. Makes triage faster.

li: agreed — that's in the ticket. Good first pass, team.
